issues.description: Method addRating(stars:) visibility differs between artifacts: the problem statement (task description) and the template declare an instance method addRating(stars:) (no access modifier) intended to be callable by client code (see problem statement task and template extension). In the solution, Course.swift defines the method as private (private func addRating(stars: Int)), while Client.swift in the solution calls swiftCourse.addRating(...). Making addRating private in the solution prevents Client.swift (a different file) from calling it, causing a compilation/access error and contradicting the exercise's expectation that clients can rate a course.
issues.suggestedFix: Make addRating(stars:) non-private in the solution (remove the private modifier) so its visibility matches the template/problem expectation and Client.swift can call it. Alternatively, if the design intends to hide the implementation, expose a public method (with the same name or a documented public wrapper) that allows clients to add ratings; document that change in the problem statement so the intended visibility is clear.
